learning_goal: Say where and when the primitive streak appears, name its parts on a drawing of the dorsal disc, describe how epiblast cells leave the surface and where they go, use the streak to give the embryo three axes, and explain the three malformations that follow when it fails to regress or fails to signal.

structures.label: Epiblast — the dorsal layer every germ layer comes from
structures.narration: Week three opens with the disc still two layers thick. Look down on it from inside the amniotic cavity and you are looking at the epiblast. Everything in this scene happens on that surface. The disc is broader at the cranial end than the caudal end, so the shape itself tells you which way round it is.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "disc_context" — carried across verbatim. In the 3D scene the surface it describes IS a built structure rather than a framing sentence.
structures.name: Epiblast — the dorsal layer every germ layer comes from

structures.label: Hypoblast — the lower layer that gets evicted
structures.narration: The lower layer of the bilaminar disc. Grey here, and shrinking in every later beat, because that is its whole story in this topic: it is pushed out of the embryonic disc by cells coming down through the streak and takes no part in the three germ layers. Watch it disappear rather than change colour — nothing here is renamed.
structures.narration_from: new — the hypoblast was described inside other structures' prose in the sequence version and needs geometry of its own here, because the whole of beat 5 turns on what happens to it.
structures.name: Hypoblast — the lower layer that gets evicted

structures.label: Primitive streak
structures.narration: On about day fifteen a narrow band thickens in the midline at the caudal end of the epiblast. That is the primitive streak. Two facts define it and both are asked: it forms in the epiblast, and it forms caudally. It then extends forwards towards the middle of the disc, so the streak is a moving structure, not a fixed line.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "streak" — carried across verbatim
structures.name: Primitive streak

structures.label: Primitive groove
structures.narration: A shallow furrow runs down the middle of the streak. That is the primitive groove, and it is simply the doorway: it is where surface cells sink out of the epiblast. If a question asks how cells get from the top layer into the middle of the disc, the answer starts at this groove.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "groove" — carried across verbatim
structures.name: Primitive groove

structures.label: Primitive node (Hensen's node)
structures.narration: The cranial end of the streak swells into a small mound — the primitive node, also called Hensen's node. Do not treat it as decoration. It is the embryo's chief organiser: the cells that build the midline pass through it, and the signals that decide which side is left come from it. Almost everything the streak does that is not simple layer-making is done here.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "node" — carried across verbatim
structures.name: Primitive node (Hensen's node)

structures.label: Primitive pit
structures.narration: A small depression sits in the centre of the node — the primitive pit. Cells destined for the midline sink here rather than at the groove, and they run forward as a tube under the ectoderm. Groove for the layers, pit for the midline: that split is the cleanest way to hold the two routes apart.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "pit" — carried across verbatim
structures.name: Primitive pit

structures.label: Definitive endoderm — epiblast that moved down and stayed
structures.narration: The lower layer of the trilaminar disc, drawn in its own colour so that the replacement can be watched happening. It spreads from the streak outwards, and the grey hypoblast ahead of it gets smaller as it goes. Every part of it entered through the groove: there is no station on this journey where a hypoblast cell joins in.
structures.narration_from: new — the sequence version taught the first wave as a route only; the 3D scene can show the layer the route builds, which is the half students are examined on.
structures.name: Definitive endoderm — epiblast that moved down and stayed

structures.label: Intraembryonic mesoderm — the middle layer
structures.narration: The middle layer, spreading sideways and forwards between the other two and thinning to nothing at its own leading edge, which is what a sheet of migrating mesenchyme does. Two things to notice: it never crosses the midline where the notochordal process lies, because it is paraxial; and it never reaches the two membranes at the ends of the disc.
structures.narration_from: new — as for the endoderm: the sequence version had the route, not the layer.
structures.name: Intraembryonic mesoderm — the middle layer

structures.label: Notochordal process — the midline route through the pit
structures.narration: Cells that enter through the pit take a different road. They run forward in the midline between ectoderm and endoderm as far as the prechordal plate and form the notochordal process, which becomes the notochord. This scene names that route because the pit has no other purpose; what the notochord then does is taught on its own.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "notochordal_process" — carried across verbatim
structures.name: Notochordal process — the midline route through the pit

structures.label: Three axes at once
structures.narration: The moment the streak appears the embryo acquires a body plan. The streak is caudal, so there is a head end and a tail end. It lies in the midline, so there is a left and a right. Ectoderm is dorsal and endoderm ventral, so there is a back and a front. Three axes from one structure, and every later description of position depends on them.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "axes" — carried across verbatim
structures.name: Three axes at once

structures.label: Two places mesoderm never reaches
structures.narration: Mesoderm spreads everywhere except two spots where ectoderm and endoderm stay stuck together. Cranially that is the oropharyngeal membrane, at the prechordal plate, and it breaks down to open the mouth. Caudally it is the cloacal membrane, which breaks down to open the anus and the urogenital opening. Both are two-layered islands in a three-layered disc, and both later have to rupture.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "membranes" — carried across verbatim
structures.name: Two places mesoderm never reaches

structures.label: How far the streak reached — the regression reference
structures.narration: Once the streak has produced enough cells it stops growing and shrinks backwards, and by about day twenty-six it has all but gone. The order it built the body in is the order it leaves: cranial structures were laid down first, caudal ones last. Two of the three malformations in this topic are simply this shrinking going wrong.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "regression" — carried across verbatim. Regression is a change over t rather than an object, so what the 3D scene gives it is a fixed reference at the streak's own high-water mark: the rails stay, the streak shrinks away from them, and the shortening becomes something a student can see rather than be told.
structures.name: How far the streak reached — the regression reference

structures.label: Nodal cilia and the leftward flow
structures.narration: Cilia on the primitive node beat in one direction and sweep signalling fluid to the left, which is how a symmetrical disc decides which side is which. If those cilia do not move, the side is settled by chance and about half of such embryos end up mirror-image — situs inversus. That is the link to Kartagener syndrome: immotile cilia give situs inversus with chronic sinusitis and bronchiectasis, and subfertility, because the same protein moves sperm tails and airway cilia.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "laterality" — carried across verbatim
structures.name: Nodal cilia and the leftward flow

structures.label: A streak that does not disappear
structures.narration: Streak cells are pluripotent, so a remnant left behind in the sacrococcygeal region can grow into a tumour containing tissue from all three germ layers — a sacrococcygeal teratoma. It is the commonest tumour of the newborn, far commoner in girls, and it is removed early because the risk of malignant change rises with age. When you are asked why it contains teeth or gut or nerve, the answer is that its parent cell had not yet chosen a layer.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "teratoma" — carried across verbatim
structures.name: A streak that does not disappear

structures.label: A streak that makes too little
structures.narration: If too little mesoderm is made at the caudal end, the structures that depend on it are deficient — sacral agenesis, imperforate anus, absent or fused kidneys, and in the extreme the lower limb buds run together as sirenomelia. This is caudal dysgenesis, and its best-known association is poorly controlled maternal diabetes. It is one of the arguments for getting glucose under control before conception rather than after a positive test.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "caudal_dysgenesis" — carried across verbatim. The model marks the caudal zone the deficiency affects; see gaps[] on what it does and does not draw.
structures.name: A streak that makes too little

structures.label: First wave — the road to the lower layer
structures.narration: The first cells through the groove push all the way down and displace the hypoblast entirely, replacing it as the definitive endoderm. Learn the direction of that sentence. The lower layer of the trilaminar disc is not the old hypoblast renamed — it is epiblast that migrated down and evicted it. Students lose this mark every year.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "endoderm_route" — carried across verbatim onto the section variant, because the median section is the only beat that draws it. See gaps[].
structures.name: First wave — the road to the lower layer

structures.label: Second wave — the road into the middle
structures.narration: The cells that follow stop between the two sheets and spread out as intraembryonic mesoderm. They fan sideways and forwards, meeting their opposite numbers in front of the prechordal plate to form the cardiogenic area. The epiblast left behind on the surface is now the ectoderm. One source, three layers, in that order.
structures.narration_from: sequence-version structure "mesoderm_route" — carried across verbatim onto the section variant, because the median section is the only beat that draws it. See gaps[].
structures.name: Second wave — the road into the middle

structures.label: Ingressing cells — the epithelial to mesenchymal transition
structures.narration: An epiblast cell reaching the groove loosens its junctions, loses E-cadherin, becomes flask-shaped and drops out of the sheet as a free mesenchymal cell. That change of state is an epithelial to mesenchymal transition, driven at the streak by FGF8, and it is the single mechanism the whole of gastrulation runs on. The same trick is reused by neural crest cells later, and by carcinoma cells when they metastasise — which is why examiners like it.

It then grows forwards, so it is a line that lengthens towards the middle of the disc.

Two doors, two destinations.

views.title: How a surface cell becomes a wandering one
views.narration: Cut across the streak and watch one cell. It reaches the groove, releases its hold on its neighbours, loses E-cadherin, narrows to a flask shape and drops out of the sheet as free mesenchyme. That is an epithelial to mesenchymal transition. It is worth a name because the embryo reuses it for neural crest, and because a carcinoma cell leaving its epithelium does exactly the same thing.

views.title: Two waves, and the mistake everyone makes
views.narration: The first cells through go all the way to the bottom and push the hypoblast out completely; what they form is the definitive endoderm. The next cells stop halfway and spread as intraembryonic mesoderm. The epiblast that never moved stays on the surface as ectoderm. So all three germ layers come from one layer, the epiblast — and the lower layer of the new disc is not the old hypoblast under a new name. That is the sentence that separates a good answer from an average one.

After it there is a craniocaudal axis, because the streak is caudal; a left and a right, because it lies in the midline; and a dorsal and a ventral surface, because ectoderm is above and endoderm below. The oropharyngeal membrane and the cloacal membrane stay two-layered and mark where the mouth and the anus will open.

views.title: Cilia on the node decide which side is left
views.narration: A symmetrical disc has to break its own symmetry. Cilia on the primitive node beat in one direction and drive fluid to the left, and the signal that collects there is what puts the heart, stomach and spleen on the left. When the cilia are immotile the choice is random, so about half of those embryos come out mirror-imaged. That is situs inversus, and paired with sinusitis, bronchiectasis and subfertility it is Kartagener syndrome — one broken motor protein, four findings.

views.narration: The streak should shrink away by about day twenty-six. Two things go wrong with that. Cells left behind in the sacrococcygeal region stay pluripotent and can grow into a sacrococcygeal teratoma — the commonest tumour of the newborn, mostly in girls, containing tissue from all three layers, and removed early because it can turn malignant. Or the streak makes too little caudal mesoderm, and you get sacral agenesis, imperforate anus, renal defects and, at the extreme, fused lower limbs. That is caudal dysgenesis, and it is the malformation most strongly linked to poorly controlled maternal diabetes — a reason to control glucose before conception, not after.

visibility_waivers.why: UNDER THE EPIBLAST, WHICH IS THE DEFINITION OF IT. Beat 1 looks down on the disc from inside the amniotic cavity, so the lower layer of a two-layered disc is behind the upper one everywhere except a sliver at the margin; it measures 0.004% of this frame. It is shown rather than hidden because the beat's first sentence is 'the disc still two layers thick' and a structure named in the narration should be in the frame it is named in, even where the camera cannot reach it. The beats that SHOW it are the two median sections: 0.328% in beat 3 and 0.186% in beat 5, both of which are about the layer it is being replaced by. A reviewer who would rather beat 1 hid it than drew it invisibly has a fair point; it is drawn because hiding it would make the parts list for that beat say the disc has one layer.

A TRANSVERSE SECTION OF THIS DISC IS A THIN SLAB, AND THIS ROUND'S FIX IS WHAT MADE THE SHORTFALL VISIBLE RATHER THAN WHAT CAUSED IT. Beat 4 cuts a slab 0.90 units thick across a disc 6.8 wide and views it from `superior`, so most of what the camera frames is the space between two laminae 0.28 and 0.16 thick: the subject's own bounding box fills 19.6% of the frame and the ink inside that box is 41% of it. BE CLEAR ABOUT THE HISTORY, because it would otherwise read as a beat that always passed and now does not. Before the round-2 fix to finding F1 this beat measured 8.02% against a floor of 8.00 — two hundredths of a percentage point of margin. The F1 fix re-solves K, dEndo and dMeso (the mesoderm's full volume falls 4.7%, from 11.705 to 11.159, because the two membrane footprints stop being mesoderm's ground), the endoderm front at this stage comes in 2.4% shorter, and the beat now measures 7.98%. The change in what a student sees is four hundredths of one percent of the frame; the change in whether the check passes is total. So this is declared rather than chased: the beat sat on the floor by construction and the fix did not move it in any way a reader could perceive. Every per-structure floor is still cleared — tv_epiblast 5.58%, tv_endoderm 1.91%, tv_streak 1.06%, tv_cells 0.72%, tv_groove 0.51%, tv_mesoderm 0.23% — so nothing in this frame is unseeable; the shortfall is the slab's aspect ratio, which is the same argument beat 5 already carries for the median section. The honest alternatives are both out of this item's reach: a tighter per-view camera fit is engine__refit-camera-on-isolate, which is ESCALATED and waiting on a human, and thickening the section to fill the frame would make this beat and the six plan-view beats disagree about one object. A reviewer who would rather see beat 4's subject narrowed to the streak and its two laminae — dropping the disc's full width from the fit, as beat 3 does to clear 17.5% without a waiver — has a real argument, and that is the change to make if this waiver is refused.

A MEDIAN SECTION OF THIS DISC IS A STRIP, AND NO CAMERA CHANGES THAT. The embryonic disc is 1.0 mm long and about 0.03 mm thick, so its median section has an aspect ratio of roughly seven to one; fitted into a square frame a 7:1 strip can fill about 14% of it at best, and the ink inside the bounding box is a little over half of that. This beat is about the LAYERS, so its camera has to hold the whole disc — beat 3, which is about the streak's own profile, isolates three pieces 4.8 units long instead of ten and clears the floor at 17.5% without a waiver, which is what tells you the shortfall here is the aspect ratio and not the composition. Its per-structure floors are all cleared — epiblast 2.11%, definitive endoderm 1.84%, mesoderm 1.82%, hypoblast 0.19% and both route arrows above the floor — and the shortfall is the strip's aspect ratio, not an occlusion. The alternative was a vertical exaggeration of the section, which is what a printed textbook does, and it was declined for a specific reason rather than on taste: six other beats draw the same disc in plan view, and a section that thickened the layers would have the two sets of beats disagreeing about one object while both claimed to be the same model. A reviewer who would rather have the exaggeration and a declared factor has a real argument and this is the place to make it.

BURIED BETWEEN THE LAYERS, WHICH IS WHERE IT IS. The notochordal process lies between the ectoderm above and the definitive endoderm below, so from the dorsal camera this beat uses it is behind the whole thickness of the epiblast; the alpha-aware pass reads it at 0.006%. It is shown here only so that the sentence 'the notochordal process you can see running forward is what the node leaves behind as it goes' has its subject present in the frame rather than referring to nothing. The beat that SHOWS it is beat 6, which takes the ectoderm away and measures it at 1.10% of the frame, and the claim about its length is asserted in both beats against the same measure.

THE BEAT'S SUBJECT IS THAT THE STREAK HAS NEARLY GONE, SO REQUIRING IT TO COVER A THIRD OF A PERCENT OF THE FRAME IS REQUIRING IT NOT TO HAVE. At t = 0.98 the streak is 0.357 units of a ten-unit disc — acceptance row F pins it at 4% of the length it reached — and its whole footprint measures 0.209% of this frame against the 0.30% floor for a structure the narration points at. The same structure measures 0.306% in beat 9, where it is still shrinking, and 7.801% in beat 2 at full extent, so the student has seen it; what this beat points at is its disappearance. The id-pick reads 0.000% rather than 0.209% because the deficiency plate is drawn over it at 0.32 opacity; the alpha-aware pass is the one that reports the real number, and the plate's opacity was lowered from 0.55 to 0.32 for exactly this reason. A reviewer who wants the relationship re-pointed from the regression rails, which measure 1.145%, has a reasonable alternative; it was not taken because a sacrococcygeal teratoma is a remnant of the STREAK and the rails are a reference rather than tissue.

THE SECTION'S PLANE DOES NOT PASS THROUGH THE BAND. Beat 3 is the median section (x = 0) and the streak BAND lies lateral to it, from |x| = GU 0.22 to SU 0.58; what the midline shows is the groove and the pit, 5.755% and 1.764% of this frame. IT MEASURED ABOVE THE FLOOR BEFORE THIS ROUND, AND THAT IS THE EVIDENCE RATHER THAN THE PROBLEM: until F3's fix there was a 0.18-unit hole in the dorsal lamina exactly where the groove hands the midline over to the pit, and the band was being seen THROUGH it. Closing the hole took those pixels away. The beats that show the band are 2 (7.343%), 8 (1.612%) and 4 (tv_streak 0.819%).

UNDER THE EPIBLAST, WHICH IS WHAT A MIDDLE LAYER IS — the same argument as beat 1's hypoblast waiver, and the same measurement. Beat 9 looks down on an intact disc from the amniotic cavity and the epiblast is 25.355% of the frame; the middle layer cannot be seen from outside it. It is shown rather than hidden because the beat narrates that the middle layer has all but finished spreading, and the claim that carries that sentence (B9-meso-done, mesoCoverFrac >= 0.93 -> 0.9556) measures the model rather than the picture. gaps: ROUTED TO 3d_anatomy, NOT TO ITS FIRST PREFERRED MODE. CURRICULUM lists preferred_modes [sequence, diagram] for this structure and declares views [mechanism, location]; both preferred modes are deferred. The reason is the queue item's own note — these twenty-eight scenes were authored for the SVG panel engine and that engine is not coming — plus the fact that the streak is a textbook procedural subject: a line that lengthens and then shortens, and two sheets built out of a third one cell at a time, so every stage is a sample of one function and no two stages can drift out of agreement. Both declared view types are carried: four beats are `mechanism` and three are `location`, with two `cross_section` and one `associated_organs` on top of them.

THE DISC IS HELD AT A FIXED SIZE AND THE REAL ONE GROWS. The embryonic disc is about 0.4 mm long when the streak appears and roughly 2 mm by the end of week three; this model draws it at 1.0 mm throughout and the growth is not modelled. The choice is deliberate and it is the one every printed figure makes: what is examined is the streak's extent AS A FRACTION of the disc — 'it reaches the middle and stops' — and a disc that grew under it would make that fraction a moving target in the picture while the geometry still satisfied it. The cost is that nothing in this scene teaches how fast the disc itself grows, and a student who takes the frames as a size comparison would be wrong. Acceptance rows E1/E2 pin the fraction at 0.598 at peak against a 0.66 ceiling.

THE HANDEDNESS OF THIS MODEL IS DECLARED AND NOT PROVED, which RENDER-STANDARD's rule 'A DECLARED AXIS IS NOT A PROVED ONE, AND A SYMMETRIC MODEL CANNOT PROVE ITS OWN' says must be recorded here rather than left to a comment. Every structure the model builds is mirror-symmetric in x — acceptance row J3 measures it and finds not one unmirrored vertex across nine sheets — EXCEPT the leftward nodal flow arrow, whose direction is a constant in models3d/primitive-streak.js and is checked against nothing outside that file. Flipping `LEFT = +x` in the header would mirror beat 8's picture, teach a rightward nodal flow and leave all 44 acceptance rows passing. The model says so itself: it exports `axesProved: false`. What this means for beat 8 is narrow and worth stating exactly: the MECHANISM it teaches — cilia beat, fluid is swept to one side, the side that collects the signal becomes the left, immotile cilia make the choice random — is not at risk, and neither is the Kartagener link. What is unproved is only that the arrow in the picture points to the student's left. Closing it needs either a landmark in this model that is independently right/left determined, or a corpus-level test of the declared axes string against a mesh-anchored model; neither exists today for a procedural model in its own units.

NOBODY HAS LOADED THIS SCENE INTO viz3d.js AND WATCHED IT. viz-training/tools/measure-scene-visibility.mjs walked all ten beats and every structure each one draws or points at is seeable, but that tool REIMPLEMENTS viz3d's ops rather than driving viz3d, and its own header says that where the two disagree viz3d is right. The adapter half IS driven by the real viz3d — 63 refs, every beat's own t and its own flags, all resolving with geometry — so what is untested is the op semantics and the per-view camera fit, not the model resolution.

BEAT 5'S FRAME IS A STRIP AND CARRIES A FRAMING WAIVER; BEAT 3'S DOES NOT. A median section of a disc 1.0 mm long and 0.03 mm thick has an aspect ratio near seven to one, and in a square frame that caps the subject at roughly 7% against the tool's 8% floor. Beat 5 is about the LAYERS so its camera must hold the whole disc, and it is waived at 6.01% with every per-structure floor cleared. Beat 3 is about the streak's own profile, so it isolates three pieces 4.8 units long rather than ten and clears the floor at 17.53% with no waiver — which is the evidence that beat 5's shortfall is the aspect ratio and not the composition. The alternative for both was a vertical exaggeration of the section, which is what a printed textbook does; it was declined because six other beats draw the same disc in plan view and an exaggerated section would have the two sets disagreeing about one object's thickness. A reviewer who would rather have the exaggeration, with the factor declared and asserted, has a real argument.

THE SECTIONS ARE ROTATED NINETY DEGREES FROM THE WAY A TEXTBOOK DRAWS THEM, and this is a corpus constraint rather than a choice. viz3d offers six canonical cameras; the median section is seen from `lateral`, which puts cranial at the top of the screen and dorsal to the right, where a printed figure puts cranial to the left and dorsal up. Nothing in the geometry is affected and no claim depends on it, but a student moving between this scene and a textbook has to turn their head.

THE TRANSVERSE SECTION IS A THICK SLAB, AND IT HAS TO BE. Beat 4 keeps the cells within 45 um of its cut plane rather than exactly in it, because a zero-thickness plane passes through no cell at all: the first version removed every cell cranial of the plane and the walk measured the ingressing cells at 0.000% of the frame on the one beat whose whole subject is an ingressing cell. A real section is tens of microns thick and the cells it shows stand proud of its face, which is what this draws. The plane itself is placed at the median y of the cells that are MID-TRANSITION at that t — measured, not nominated — so the beat cannot show six cells and not one of them flask-shaped. Claim B4-flask-in-section asserts exactly that.

THE NUMBER OF CELLS IS NOT A NUMBER OF CELLS. Twenty-six cells cross the streak over the whole of this model's clock and between five and ten are in transit at any stage. The real figure is orders of magnitude larger and is not knowable from this geometry. What the cells are for is the ROUTE and the SHAPE CHANGE — which door, which destination, and the flask profile — and claims B4-cells, B4-cells-in-section, B4-flask and B4-left-sheet are all about those. A count is never narrated.

THE TWO ROUTE ARROWS REPLACE TWO TRACE_STRUCTURE OPS, and that is a capability gap rather than an authoring choice. The sequence version's beats 4 and 5 traced `concept:ingressing-cells` and `concept:midline-migration`; viz3d's procedural adapter degrades TRACE_STRUCTURE to a highlight because a procedural model exposes no centreline for the player to walk. The arrows are built on the SAME path function the cells travel, resampled by arc length, so the road a student follows and the cells they watch cannot disagree — but the player draws them as objects rather than animating along them, so the motion the trace would have given is lost.

THE UNCUT `ingression`, `endoderm_route` AND `mesoderm_route` ARE BUILT BY THE MODEL AND NAMED BY NO BEAT. They were authored as structures first and removed: from the dorsal camera the cells in the groove are three specks and both arrows are seen end-on, and the harness reported all three as shown in no beat. Their sequence-version narration is carried verbatim onto the section variants that DO draw them — tv_cells, sec_endo_route, sec_meso_route — so no teaching was lost, and acceptance row S asserts the model still builds all three, so a later beat can take them without touching the model.

THE `dysgenesis` VARIANT IS BUILT, PROVED AND DRAWN BY NO BEAT. The model can build a mesoderm with its caudal third missing and acceptance row W2 measures the coverage falling by 0.247 when it is switched on, but beat 10 draws the deficient ZONE as a marked plate over the normal mesoderm instead. The reason is the visibility walk: a beat showing a deficient mesoderm shows an absence, and an absence has no pixels to measure. The plate's area is pinned by claim B10-deficit between a fifth and two fifths of the disc. A reviewer who wants beat 10 to use the variant — or to add an eleventh beat comparing the two mesoderms side by side — has a reasonable case and the model already supports it.

THE CONSERVATION IS EXACT IN A PLANAR MEASURE. Every volume the model solves against is a quadrature of dx dy on the midsurface's projection, which ignores the disc's 0.26-unit dorsal convexity and so understates the true surface area by about 0.2%. The same measure is used for the delivery and for all three built layers, so the conservation it enforces is exact in the measure it is stated in — acceptance row C reports a worst residual of 3.5e-9 across thirteen stages — and the perturbation battery uses the dome as its NEGATIVE control for exactly this reason: moving the convexity must change the picture and must NOT change a solved volume, and it does not.

BELOW t = 0.15 THE SOLVED FRONTS ARE NOT MONOTONE, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A PICTURE. At those stages the streak is shorter than one row of the quadrature grid, so which row centres fall inside its span changes as it grows and the front radius needed to hold a monotone volume genuinely falls. Acceptance row M1 asserts the monotone thing — the built VOLUMES, over 301 stages, exactly — and row M3 pins the mesoderm at that point at under one ten-thousandth of its final volume. No beat goes near it; the earliest is t = 0.20.

A RENDER-KIT DEFECT WAS FOUND AND IS REPORTED RATHER THAN FIXED. A kit tube whose radius function reaches EXACTLY zero at one end, capped at the other, comes back non-manifold at the capped rim — three triangles on every rim edge. The mechanism: sweptShell writes a solid tube's flat end discs through triN, which drops a degenerate triangle, so a zero-radius end gets no disc; stripFlatCap then fails its own `pos.count === hull + 6 * ring` assertion and returns the geometry UNSTRIPPED, leaving the start's flat disc coincident under the start's dome. That is precisely the defect tubeCapped was written to remove — render-kit's own comment calls it 'a one-pixel dark ellipse round every capped end' — reappearing wherever a tube comes to a point, which is every arrowhead in this corpus. Section 10b of viz-training/tools/render-primitive-streak.mjs reproduces it in five lines with no model code and keeps a positive control beside it. It is NOT fixed here because render-kit is shared by every model and that is a review's decision. This model stays off the shape instead: its arrowheads are blunted to 6% of their own radius, which the probe measures as clean and which is 1.3 um on screen.

ROUND-3 FINDING F3 IS CLOSED, AND HERE IS WHAT IT ACTUALLY WAS. The hole in the dorsal surface was NOT in regionsAt()'s medial lane boundaries, which is where round 3 placed it: the partition is exact at every row centre (row P1 passes on the unfixed file, and a lane-by-lane sweep of all 56 rows at nine values of t finds no uncovered micron). It was in the SWEEP. Each region was built from its first row centre to its last, so wherever the part owning a column changed from one row to the next — groove to pit, pit to epiblast — both runs stopped at their own row centres and the row-wide strip between them belonged to nobody. The y-boundaries of this model's parts are ellipse rims and named landmarks and not one of them lands on a row centre. The fix: the dorsal lamina's five central parts and the epiblast are now swept over a SHARED STATION SET that carries, besides every row centre, a station on every y where any of them appears or disappears, each found by bisecting the lane itself; a part that stops abruptly does it as a run boundary with coincident end caps rather than as a very short sweep. MEASURED: at t=0.44 the four parts now tile y exactly — streak [-3.65, 0.073], groove [-3.65, -0.12], node and pit [-0.12, 1.12] — against the analytic landmarks yNodeCaud = -0.12 and yTip + NOD_RY = 1.12, where before they stopped at row centres 0.03 to 0.14 short. A ray probe at 0.005-unit spacing along y and thirteen columns in x, over ten values of t, finds NO column of the disc without dorsal lamina except at the two membranes' rims (below). Row P3 is the standing check, and the harness's rowsOnly control re-creates the old construction from the live file and requires P3 to fail on it, which it does. On the reviewer's own test — background-coloured pixels enclosed by the disc in beat08_posterior.png — 925 before, 49 after, and all 49 at the membranes' rims rather than cranial of the node.

AND WHAT F3'S FIX DOES NOT REACH, MEASURED RATHER THAN ESTIMATED, BECAUSE IT IS THE SAME DEFECT ELSEWHERE. (a) THE MEMBRANES' RIMS: the membranes and the ventral lamina are still swept on row centres, so the handover from a membrane to the epiblast and to the endoderm still spreads over a whole row. Row P3 counts it every run (68 columns of 6,007 at four values of t, all within one row of a rim or of the disc's own tip) and it is the 49 enclosed pixels in beat 8. (b) THE VENTRAL LAMINA generally: the same ray probe finds 220 to 753 uncovered columns per t on the ventral side, at the membranes' rims, at the mesoderm front's leading rim and at the disc's cranial margin. (c) THE DISC'S OWN TIPS: every sheet still ends at the outermost row centre, so the disc is built 9.82 long against the 10.00 its outline declares. WHY NONE OF THE THREE WAS TAKEN HERE, which is a geometry problem and not a scheduling one: each membrane's footprint is a circle, so AT ITS RIM THE BOUNDARY RUNS ACROSS THE SWEEP, and a station there makes the interval below it carry the whole closure — the endoderm's inner edge travels 0.213 in x across 0.038 in y. On the dorsal side the height field is smooth there and the quads survive row N; on the ventral side the mesoderm's fade ramp meets the same rim and 2 of the endoderm's 5,288 triangles at t=0.98 wind against their own normals (row N, 0.99962). Row N is the row that caught the original winding bug and it does not get a threshold. Four ways round it were tried and measured: midpoint refinement makes it WORSE (44 offending triangles at seven passes, endoderm triangles tripled), taking the normal's y-slope from the mesh's own secant makes it worse (15), choosing the other diagonal of the sheared quad does not reach it, and truncating the footprint to turn the rim into a step needs the truncation to reach 0.163 of the radius before the shear is bounded, which flattens a membrane a beat points at. What it needs is a sweeper whose two adjacent stations may carry DIFFERENT numbers of samples across the lane, so a boundary running across the sweep is met by a fan rather than by shearing every quad in the row. That is a change to how every sheet in this model is built and it is proposed here rather than made at the end of a build run.

The visibility walk asks the opposite question — whether each structure a beat draws can be seen — and a hole is not a structure, so neither tool has a side that fails. PROPOSED RULE, which is round 3's proposal (1) made concrete and should be a tool rather than a reviewer's lattice: EVERY BEAT IS CHECKED FOR WHAT IT DOES NOT DRAW. For each beat, at its own t and flags, count the columns where the model has lamina geometry and the beat's shown set has none; the count is zero or it is declared with its size and its owner. STRUCTURAL NOTE, NOT FIXED HERE AND THE REASON THIS KEEPS RECURRING: the partition gives each sub-part exclusive ownership of its footprint, so the epiblast is not a continuous sheet that the groove, node and pit sit in — it is a sheet with holes cut in it that those parts plug. Every beat must therefore carry the whole plug set or draw a hole, and every new sub-part repeats this. A model in which the epiblast owns its full footprint and the sub-parts are drawn over it would make the defect unreachable instead of re-fixable. That is a build decision and is left to one.

Beat 7's sentence names the endoderm and beat 10's names the mesoderm, so those two are waived with their figures. Beat 7's mesoderm and notochordal_process are named nowhere in its narration, carry no HIGHLIGHT_STRUCTURE or SHOW_RELATIONSHIP, and draw zero pixels, so they are HIDDEN rather than argued for — removing two SHOW_STRUCTURE ops that change not one pixel of the frame. Both remain shown in beats that do draw them (mesoderm in 6, 9 and 10; notochordal_process in 6 and 9), so no structure in this scene is drawn by no beat. The builder's own warning on its four waivers — 'a reviewer should read them as four arguments and reject any that does not hold' — is the standard applied here to the reviewer's own.

ROUND-4 FINDING F5 IS OPEN AND ESCALATED, AND IT IS THE REASON F2 AND F4 KEEP HAPPENING. The sectioned beats have the same defect as the plan-view ones and ONE OF THEM CANNOT BE FIXED FROM THE SCENE AT ALL. MEASURED on the built triangles of the cut model, 0.1-unit lattice, columns where the model has dorsal lamina and the beat's own shown set has none: beat 3 (cutx, t 0.44) 48 columns, owner `node`; beat 5 (cutx, t 0.52) 293 columns — streak 109, groove 105, node 48, pit 31; beat 4 (cuty, t 0.33) 0. Beat 3's is closed this round by adding sec_node, the one dorsal part that had no section variant. BEAT 5'S CANNOT BE. Its subject is the two waves, carried by sec_endo_route and sec_meso_route, and the parts that own the dorsal lamina on the median plane are exactly the parts that stand in front of those arrows from the lateral camera. Drawing them closes the lamina and buries the beat: measured both ways, with sec_streak, sec_groove, sec_node and sec_pit added the walk reads sec_endo_route 0.033 -> 0.010 and sec_meso_route 0.027 -> 0.003, both under the floor, and dropping sec_streak and keeping only the three midline parts gives the identical 0.010 and 0.003 — so it is the groove and the pit on the midline, not the band, and there is no subset that closes the gap and keeps the beat. The scene is left with beat 5 as it was, the gap open and declared, rather than with its own teaching content occluded. WHY IT IS A DECISION AND NOT A DEFECT: the model's partition gives each sub-part EXCLUSIVE, OPAQUE ownership of its footprint, so the epiblast is not a sheet the groove and node sit in — it is a sheet with holes cut in it that they plug. Every beat must therefore carry the whole plug set or draw a hole, and on beat 5 carrying the plug set and teaching the beat are mutually exclusive. Rounds 3 (F2, membranes), 4 (F4, groove/node/pit in plan view) and 4 (F5, the sections) are three instances of that one cause, each found only by someone going looking for it. The fix is a build decision and there are two: give the section's dorsal parts their own opacity so beat 5 can draw them and still show the arrows through them, which gap 14 already says needs a structure and a model flag of its own; or make the epiblast own its full footprint and draw the sub-parts over it, which makes the whole class unreachable instead of re-fixable. The second is the larger change and the one that stops this recurring. Neither is a reviewer's call.
